title: Elige el mundo visual
question: The roll assigned El Albarán. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: El Albarán
options.lineage: Printed delivery notes (albaranes) and order pads from the shop counter
options.thesis: Every task is a numbered delivery note, filled in blue ink and stamped when its state changes.
materials: printed form rules and labeled fields
options.viewport: Phone, Mis tareas: a stack of slips ordered by deadline under a HOY rule; each slip has Nº, a large title, labeled fields and a full-width status button at its foot.
options.risk: Tips into skeuomorphic pastiche if the rules and stamps are decoration instead of state.

raised.raise: Fields are edited in place on the slip: reading it and filling it in are the same object.
Each color keeps exactly one law: blue is ink and action, red is only lateness and urgency.
One vertical time axis with a HOY rule orders Mis tareas; everything above the rule is late.
On phones the board's columns become snap rails, one estado per screen with the next peeking in.
A state change re-stamps the slip in place; the grid never reflows.

options.label: La Placa
options.lineage: The JC Confort badge and shop sign: blue frame, red base band
options.thesis: The logo's framed badge becomes the app's structure: blue-framed panels, a red band only where something is wrong.
options.viewport: Phone: a blue framed header plate with the badge, then task plates with a thick left frame colored by estado.
options.risk: Familiar: the closest to a straight brand skin, and where most restyles in this category land.

options.label: Pase de reparto
options.lineage: Boarding pass and departures gate board
options.thesis: Each task is a segmented pass; Mis tareas is a departures board ranked by deadline.
options.viewport: Phone: a board of my tasks ranked by time; a changed row glows its alert color until seen.
options.case: Very clear for scanning by deadline; loses on identification because the team lives with albaranes, not airports.
options.risk: Reads as a travel app when it is not tied to deliveries.

options.label: Panel de salidas
options.thesis: Tasks as departure rows with flipping letters.
options.case: Dark, theatrical ground fights older readers and the family-shop feel.
options.kept: State restyles a row without breaking the grid.

options.label: HyperCard stack
options.thesis: Cards you browse and author in one mode.
options.case: One-bit black and white erases the brand's blue and red.
options.kept: Read and edit are the same object: in-place editing.

options.label: Gravity rain garden
options.thesis: Color codes the direction of every force.
options.case: No task clarity and nothing the team recognizes.
options.kept: Every color obeys exactly one law.

options.label: Deep dive
options.thesis: One vertical depth axis rules every line.
options.case: Dark oceanic world has no link to a furniture shop.
options.kept: One vertical time axis orders everything.

options.label: Streaming wall
options.case: Tasks have no artwork; dark entertainment feel is wrong.
options.kept: Snap rails: one column per screen on phones.

canonCard.label: El estándar
canonCard.thesis: A clean Trello-style board in brand blue, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar with logo, columns of rounded cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any task app by design.
